verdict.rationale: The docs describe how multiparty sessions behave as they grow: the Media Router cuts bandwidth, supports scalable video and more mobile clients, and the SDKs switch transparently between peer-to-peer and Media Router relaying. However, no evidence states how many participants or viewers a single session supports. Missing for 10: documented per-session participant/viewer limits, explicit thresholds for when the relay switch happens, broadcast/viewer scale figures, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the vendor documents how many participants or viewers one session supports and what changes as a session grows

citations.quote: The Media Router can decrease bandwidth usage in multiparty sessions.
The switch between peer-to-peer relaying and Media Router relaying is handled transparently by the client SDKs.
Scalable video can greatly improve the quality of video in multi-party sessions.
The Media Router supports additional clients for multiparty sessions on mobile devices.
